item.research_question: How can high-entropy alloy (HEA) nanocatalysts be synthesized to achieve simultaneous high performance for both hydrogen evolution (HER) and methanol oxidation (MOR) reactions, and what is the mechanism behind their enhanced activity and stability?
item.material_system: Pt18Ni26Fe15Co14Cu27 high-entropy alloy nanoparticles supported on carbon (Pt18Ni26Fe15Co14Cu27/C)
item.processing_route: One-pot oil phase synthesis at 220 °C for 2 hours at atmospheric pressure using metal acetylacetonate precursors, oleylamine, CTAC, glucose, and Mo(CO)6, followed by acetic acid treatment to remove surfactants and dispersion on Ketjen Black-300 carbon.
item.test_conditions: HER tested in N2-saturated 1 M KOH (LSV scan rate 5 mV s−1, stability via chronoamperometry at 11 mV and 10,000 CV cycles); MOR tested in N2-saturated 1 M KOH + 1 M CH3OH (CV scan rate 20 mV s−1, stability via chronoamperometry at 0.65 V and 1,000 CV cycles).
key_findings: The Pt18Ni26Fe15Co14Cu27/C catalyst exhibits an ultrasmall overpotential of 11 mV at a current density of 10 mA cm−2 for HER, compared to 84 mV for commercial Pt/C.
The mass activity for HER is 10.96 A mg−1Pt at −0.07 V vs. RHE, significantly higher than the 0.83 A mg−1Pt of commercial Pt/C.
The catalyst achieves a mass activity of 15.04 A mg−1Pt for MOR, which is 10 times higher than that of Pt/C (1.45 A mg−1Pt).
The catalyst maintains 99% of its current density after 10 hours of chronoamperometry at 11 mV, whereas Pt/C retains only ~53%.
After 10,000 CV cycles, the Pt18Ni26Fe15Co14Cu27/C catalyst shows no obvious negative shift in overpotential, while Pt/C shifts by ~33 mV.
The Tafel slope for HER is 30 mV dec−1 for the HEA catalyst compared to 98 mV dec−1 for Pt/C, indicating faster kinetics.
CO stripping onset potential is 0.391 V vs. RHE for the HEA catalyst, a 181 mV decrease compared to Pt/C (0.572 V), indicating superior CO anti-poisoning.
DFT calculations reveal a low activation barrier of 0.11 eV for water dissociation and a rate-determining step energy barrier of 0.45 eV for MOR.
item.mechanism: The authors attribute the performance to a synergistic effect of multi-active sites on the HEA surface, where different elements (Pt, Ni, Fe, Co, Cu) facilitate specific steps: Pt acts as an electron reservoir, Ni and Co dominate the electroactive region near the Fermi level for electron depletion, and Fe stabilizes intermediates. This configuration enables fast site-to-site electron transfer, efficient water dissociation, and optimal binding strength for intermediates, while the lattice distortion and multi-component nature inhibit CO poisoning and structural degradation.
item.limitations: The text notes that slight stoichiometry variations (e.g., changing Cu content) lead to slightly lower activity, though the optimal composition is robust; it also mentions that non-noble metals (Ni, Fe, Co, Cu) may leach slightly during electrocatalysis, causing minor stoichiometry variations, although the overall structure remains stable.
item.future_work: The authors propose that the simple oil phase synthesis strategy and the understanding of the multi-active sites and fast site-to-site electron transfer mechanism will lay the foundation for the preparation of other HEAs and their application in related electrocatalysis.
quotes: The Pt18Ni26Fe15Co14Cu27/C catalyst exhibits excellent electrocatalytic performance for hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) and methanol oxidation reaction (MOR).
The construction of HEA surfaces supplies the fast site-to-site electron transfer for both reduction and oxidation processes.
The synergistic effect of multi-active sites on the HEA surface determines the remarkable performance of HER and MOR.
